text:
maria.g: Quick sanity check from the NovaX-12B int4 bring-up. ran perf + eval on the headline/longform suites yesterday. cost down ~48% vs fp16 but we're seeing a noticeable quality cliff on multi-paragraph summarization slices. samples attached in the report.
aj: can you paste the short signal summary here? main slices affected?
maria.g: Short: long-form QA & summarization (>=3 paragraphs) show ROUGE drop ~7-9 pts; single-paragraph and Q/A flashcards are fine. latency and throughput are great though. unit econ looks attractive for chat use-cases.
neil: is the regression correlated with sequence length or with specific tokens/formatting (e.g., bullet lists)?
maria.g: Mostly sequence length and context-window reuse. We see the attention KV cache behaves slightly differently in int4, leading to hallucination spikes when prompts contain lots of numbered lists.
eva: any ablation between group-wise quant and per-channel? might be a qconfig artifact.
maria.g: We tested two qconfigs: `group=128, sym=True, calibr=mlq` and `group=64, sym=False, calibr=percentile`. The 64-group helped recall a bit but still below baseline. paste of the small config we used:

```
quant_config = {
  "precision": "int4",
  "group_size": 64,
  "symmetric": false,
  "calibration": "percentile",
}
```

aj: thanks. what's the traffic plan recommendation? full rollout would cut cost but risk product regressions.
neil: suggest mixed-fleet: default route shorter/single-turn to NovaX-int4, fallback for long-form requests to NovaX-int8 or fp16. plus shadow traffic for int4 on long-form to collect more metrics.
eva: agree. also add prompt-sanitization / canonicalization to reduce list-formatting variance. maybe a prefix that flattens numbered lists before sending to int4.
maria.g: I'm +1 on mixed-fleet. quick estimated econ: for our chat slice (60% of calls) int4 saves ~52% cost -> net org savings ~30% if we route 60% traffic. adding fallback for long-form brings savings down to ~22% but keeps quality at parity.
aj: ok. what signals do we use to auto-route? length alone or model-estimated difficulty?
neil: start with simple heuristics: token_count > 1024 -> route to int8/fp16; tokens <= 1024 -> int4. Add a small ML classifier later using past error rates.
eva: operational checklist:
- canary: 5% traffic for 72h with full eval hooks
- shadow long-form on int4 (store outputs) for 7 days
- enable per-prompt rollup metrics (ROUGE, perplexity, hallucination rate)
- create a rollback policy if long-form recall drop >5 pts on production samples
maria.g: I'll draft the canary plan and a short eval harness for the shadowing. blocker: need a way to tag requests as "longform" at routing time (product help needed). @aj can you coordinate with product on tagging?
aj: yep, will ping @product in the morning and propose a header `X-Redwood-Mode: longform`.
ops-bot: deploy scheduled: `novax-int4-canary` -> starts 2026-03-24T02:00Z, 5%.
maria.g: perfect. final note: if we want more cost upside later, re-run with per-channel quantization and a small distillation pass for long-form only. but that's phase 2.
eva: sounds good. i'll add the prompt-flattening snippet to the infra repo and wire up metric dashboards.
neil: let's also include a small human eval batch (50 samples) for longform before canary.
aj: thanks team. i'll follow up on product tagging + schedule a short sync tomorrow.
maria.g: thanks all :thumbsup:
